concepts.name: President: eligibility, electoral college, election, term and impeachment
concepts.description: Articles 52 to 62 on the office of the President: qualifications, the electoral college, weighted votes and STV, term, oath, impeachment, vacancy and the rules of business.
concepts.idea: The President is elected indirectly by elected MPs and MLAs on a weighted STV ballot, holds office for five years, and can be removed only by impeachment for violation of the Constitution.
concepts.rule: The Union executive (President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers and Attorney General) is dealt with in Articles 52 to 78 of Part V. A presidential candidate must be a citizen of 35 years, qualified for the Lok Sabha and holding no office of profit. The electoral college has the elected members of both Houses, of the State Legislative Assemblies and, since the 70th Amendment (1992), of the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies; nominated members and Legislative Council members are excluded. Votes are weighted on the 1971 population (frozen by the 84th Amendment until the first Census after 2026), the winner needs more than half of valid vote value through transfers, and the term is five years from entering office with unlimited re-election. Impeachment for violation of the Constitution needs a resolution signed by one-fourth of a House, 14 days' notice and two-thirds of the total membership of each House; on a vacancy the Vice-President, then the Chief Justice, acts and an election follows within six months.
concepts.example: In a first count where no candidate has the quota, the last-placed candidate is eliminated and his votes pass on, so a trailing candidate can still win.

questions.q: Part V of the Constitution devotes Articles 52 to 78 to the Union executive. Which Article opens the series by providing that there shall be a President of India?
questions.e: Article 52 says there shall be a President of India (Laxmikanth p.276 and its table of Articles on p.295).
w: Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President; it does not create the office.
Article 54 lays down the election of the President.
Article 56 fixes the President's term of office.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution makes a person who holds or has held the office of President eligible for re-election?
questions.e: Article 57 provides eligibility for re-election, with no cap on the number of terms (Laxmikanth p.281 and p.295).
w: Article 56 deals with the five-year term, not re-election.
Article 58 lists the qualifications for election as President.
Article 59 deals with the conditions of the President's office.

questions.q: A President-elect makes an oath or affirmation under Article 60 before entering office. If the Chief Justice of India is not available, the oath is administered by
questions.a: the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available
o: the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available
the Vice-President, who ranks next to the President
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, as head of the popularly elected House
the Attorney General of India, as the first law officer of the Union
questions.e: The Chief Justice administers the oath and, in his absence, the senior-most Supreme Court judge available does (Laxmikanth p.280).
w: The Vice-President does not administer this oath; he himself takes his oath before the President.
The Speaker has no role in administering the presidential oath.
The Attorney General has no role in administering the presidential oath.

questions.q: The value of an MLA's vote in the presidential election is worked out from the population of the State. According to the 84th Amendment Act, 2001, the Census figures used for this purpose stay those of 1971 until
questions.a: the figures of the first Census taken after 2026 are published
o: the figures of the first Census taken after 2026 are published
the figures of the 2011 Census are published
the next Delimitation Commission submits its report
the first Census taken after 2001 is completed in full
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.277 footnote 2) says the 1971 population is used until the first Census after 2026 is published, so that States which controlled population are not penalised.
w: The 84th Amendment looked beyond 2011; the freeze was extended past it.
Delimitation reports are not the trigger; the Amendment ties the freeze to Census publication.
The Amendment moved the base year forward to 2026, not to the next Census after 2001.

questions.q: The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and of Puducherry were brought into the electoral college for the presidential election by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.e: The 70th Amendment Act, 1992 added them (Laxmikanth p.276 footnote 1).
w: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18; it did not touch the electoral college.
The 73rd Amendment of the same year inserted Part IX on Panchayats.
The 84th Amendment froze the 1971 population base; it did not add the Union Territories.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the qualifications for election as President:

1. The candidate must be an Indian citizen who has completed 35 years of age.
2. Qualification for election to the Lok Sabha is a pre-condition for standing in the presidential election.
3. A Governor of a State is deemed to hold an office of profit and so cannot stand for President.
4. A Union or State Minister is not deemed to hold an office of profit and so may be a candidate.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Both conditions are laid down (Laxmikanth p.280). Statement 2 is correct: This is the third qualification (Laxmikanth p.280). Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 58 a Governor is not deemed to hold an office of profit, and neither are the President, Vice-President or a Union or State Minister. Statement 4 is correct: A Minister of the Union or of a State is expressly excluded from the office-of-profit bar (Laxmikanth p.280). So the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.60
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.60
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.60

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the electoral college for the election of the President:

1. The elected members of both Houses of Parliament are part of the electoral college.
2. The nominated members of Parliament are also part of the electoral college, but without a weighted vote.
3. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are included, as a result of the 70th Amendment Act, 1992.
4. The elected members of a State Legislative Council take part when the State has a bicameral legislature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: They are listed first among the electors (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 2 is incorrect: Nominated members of both Houses are excluded altogether. Statement 3 is correct: They were brought in by that Amendment. Statement 4 is incorrect: Members of State Legislative Councils, elected or nominated, do not take part in the election (Laxmikanth p.276). So the answer is 1 and 3 only.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.60
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.60
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.60

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the value of votes in the presidential election:

1. Article 55 supplements Article 54 and aims at parity between the States as a whole and the Union through weighted votes.
2. An MLA from a State with a larger population per elected seat casts a vote of higher value.
3. The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 freezes the population base at the 1971 Census until the first Census after 2026 is published.
4. The value of an MP's vote equals the value of an MLA's vote in the State from which the MP is elected.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: This is the stated aim of Article 55 (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 2 is correct: The value is the population divided by the number of elected members, in multiples of one thousand, so more people per seat means a higher value (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 3 is correct: The freeze is stated in the and Laxmikanth p.277 footnote 2. Statement 4 is incorrect: An MP's vote is the total value of all MLAs' votes divided by the number of elected MPs, so it is the same for every MP (700 in 2022) and differs from an MLA's value (Laxmikanth p.277 and p.299). So the answer is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.60
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.60
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.60

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the way a President is elected:

1. If no candidate reaches the quota, the votes of the candidate with the fewest first preferences are cancelled and not transferred.
2. The elector marks candidates in order of preference as 1, 2, 3 and so on.
3. Since only one post is to be filled, the winner needs more than 50 per cent of the total valid vote value as the quota.
4. Voting in the presidential election is by secret ballot.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Those votes are transferred according to their next preferences. Statement 2 is correct: This is how the single transferable vote works (Laxmikanth p.277). Statement 3 is correct: The quota is more than half of valid votes (Laxmikanth p.277). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.277 describe proportional representation by the single transferable vote with a secret ballot. So the answer is 2, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.61
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.61
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.61

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's term and oath:

1. The five-year term runs from the date of the election result.
2. The President may resign at any time by writing to the Vice-President.
3. A person who has been President may be re-elected for one further term, and no more.
4. A person acting as President or discharging presidential functions is not required to take an oath or affirmation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Under Article 56(1) the term runs from the date the President enters upon office. Statement 2 is correct: The resignation is addressed to the Vice-President (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 57 sets no limit on the number of terms. Statement 4 is incorrect: Such a person takes a similar oath or affirmation (Laxmikanth p.280). So the answer is 2 only.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.61
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.61
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.61

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the impeachment of the President:

1. Article 61 spells out what amounts to a violation of the Constitution, the sole ground for impeachment.
2. A charge is moved as a resolution signed by at least one-fourth of the total members of the House, after 14 days' notice to the President.
3. Nominated members of Parliament take part in the impeachment although they do not vote in the election of the President.
4. The second House investigates the charge, but the President has no right to appear or to be represented there.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution does not define the phrase. Statement 2 is correct: A charge is moved as a resolution signed by at least one-fourth of the total members of the House, after 14 days' notice to the President (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 3 is correct: Only MPs, elected and nominated, take part (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 4 is incorrect: The President has the right to appear and to be represented at the investigation. So the answer is 2 and 3 only.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.61
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.61
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.61

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a vacancy in the office of President:

1. On a vacancy in the President's office, the Vice-President acts as President.
2. If the Vice-President's office is also vacant, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha acts as President.
3. The person elected to fill a vacancy serves the unexpired part of the predecessor's term.
4. An election to fill a vacancy caused by death or resignation must be held within six months.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: On a vacancy in the President's office, the Vice-President acts as President (Laxmikanth p.282). Statement 2 is incorrect: The Chief Justice of India acts, or, if he is unavailable, the senior-most Supreme Court judge. Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 62 the person elected gets a full fresh term of five years (Laxmikanth p.282). Statement 4 is correct: Article 62 sets the six-month limit (Laxmikanth p.282). So the answer is 1 and 4 only.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.61
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.61
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.61

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the conduct of Union government business:

1. The Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961 operationalise Article 77 and are framed under Article 77(3).
2. The Cabinet Committees under the Rules mainly decide judicial appointments and Fundamental Rights petitions.
3. The Ministry of Law must be consulted on legislative proposals, on framing of rules and orders, and on drafting contracts for the Government.
4. The Rules set up a system of Cabinet Committees to streamline decision-making.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.283 (the President makes rules for more convenient transaction of business). Statement 2 is incorrect: They mainly deal with national security, economic affairs, appointments and parliamentary matters. Statement 3 is correct: The Ministry of Law must be consulted on legislative proposals, on framing of rules and orders, and on drafting contracts for the Government. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.324 says the Rules of Business provide for their establishment. So the answer is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.61
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.61
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.61

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union executive:

1. The Union executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister and the Attorney General of India.
2. The Constitutional provisions on the Union executive are in Articles 52 to 78 of Part V.
3. Article 52 provides that there shall be a President of India.
4. The President is the head of the Indian State and acts as a symbol of the unity, integrity and solidarity of the nation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Union executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister and the Attorney General of India (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 2 is correct: The Constitutional provisions on the Union executive are in Articles 52 to 78 of Part V (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 3 is correct: Article 52 provides that there shall be a President of India (Laxmikanth p.295). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.276 describes the President as head of the State, first citizen of India and symbol of national unity. So the answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.60
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.60
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.60

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the presidential electoral college and candidates:

1. Nominated members of State Legislative Assemblies have no vote in the presidential election.
2. The nominated members of the Puducherry Legislative Assembly are also excluded.
3. Fifty electors must propose and fifty second a presidential nomination.
4. A candidate for the presidency must lodge a security deposit of Rs 15,000 with the Reserve Bank of India.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: They are excluded (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.276 states this; Delhi's Assembly has no nominated members. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280, after the 1997 increase from ten each. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280 gives the deposit as Rs 15,000 at the Reserve Bank of India. So all four statements are correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about removal and replacement of a President:

1. Impeachment may be initiated in the Lok Sabha but not in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The first House must pass the impeachment resolution by two-thirds of its total membership.
3. If the second House also passes the resolution by two-thirds of its total membership, the President stands removed.
4. The President may be impeached on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It may be initiated in either House (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 2 is correct: The first House must pass the impeachment resolution by two-thirds of its total membership (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 3 is correct: If the second House also passes the resolution by two-thirds of its total membership, the President stands removed (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 4 is incorrect: The sole ground is violation of the Constitution (Article 61; Laxmikanth p.281). So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the four statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the four statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the four statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rules of business:

1. Article 77(3) empowers the President to frame rules for the convenient transaction of Union business and for allocating subjects among ministers.
2. The Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961 were enacted by Parliament as a statute.
3. The Ministry of Law is consulted on legislative proposals but not on the framing of rules and orders.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 77(3) empowers the President to frame rules for the convenient transaction of Union business and for allocating subjects among ministers (Laxmikanth p.316). Statement 2 is incorrect: They are rules made by the President under Article 77(3), not an Act of Parliament. Statement 3 is incorrect: Consultation covers legislative proposals, framing of rules and orders, and drafting of contracts. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A candidate who is behind at the first count of preferences can still be elected President.
Statement-II: If no candidate reaches the quota, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and his votes pass to the remaining candidates by next preference, and this is repeated until someone reaches the quota.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: and Statement-II explains it: transferred preferences can lift a trailing candidate over the quota (Laxmikanth p.277).
w: Statement-II is the actual reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The members of State Legislative Assemblies take no part in the impeachment of the President although they vote in his election.
Statement-II: The nominated members of Parliament are excluded from the impeachment of the President because they are excluded from his election.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: only Members of Parliament take part in impeachment (Laxmikanth p.281-282). Statement-II is incorrect: nominated MPs do take part in impeachment even though they do not vote in the election (Laxmikanth p.281).
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is not correct, so the 'both correct' options fail.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the Articles in List-I with the subjects in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 55
B. Article 56
C. Article 57
D. Article 60

List-II
1. Eligibility for re-election
2. Oath or affirmation by the President
3. Term of office
4. Manner of election
questions.e: Article 55 prescribes the manner of election; Article 56 the five-year term (p.61); Article 57 re-election (p.61); Article 60 the oath (p.61). Also in Laxmikanth p.295.
w: A and B are interchanged: Article 55 prescribes the manner of election and Article 56 the term.
C and D are interchanged: Article 57 concerns re-election and Article 60 the oath.
B and C are interchanged: Article 56 fixes the term and Article 57 re-election.

concepts.name: Council's advice, appointments, Parliament, assent and the types of veto
concepts.description: Article 74 and Article 78, the President's appointments, his role in summoning Parliament and addressing it, assent to Bills and the absolute, suspensive, pocket and qualified vetoes.
concepts.idea: The President acts on ministerial advice, appoints the high officers of the Union, and may assent to, withhold or return a Bill, with no time limit on a Bill reserved by a Governor.
concepts.rule: Under Article 74 the President acts on the Council's advice and may return it once; Article 78 makes the Prime Minister the channel of information. The President appoints the Prime Minister, judges, the Attorney General, CAG, Governors, Election Commissioners and others, nominates 12 Rajya Sabha members and decides disqualification of MPs on the Election Commission's opinion. He addresses Parliament under Articles 86 and 87, and the Motion of Thanks follows. Under Article 111 he may assent, withhold or return a Bill (not a Money Bill); a re-passed Bill must be assented to, a Constitution Amendment Bill must be assented to (24th Amendment, 1971), and a reserved State Bill need not be assented to even if re-passed. India has the absolute, suspensive and pocket vetoes but no qualified veto.
concepts.example: A Money Bill introduced on the President's recommendation cannot be returned to Parliament; he can only assent or withhold assent.

questions.q: Under Article 74 the President may send a recommendation of the Council of Ministers back for reconsideration. If the Council repeats its advice, the President
questions.a: is bound by the advice as repeated after reconsideration
o: is bound by the advice as repeated after reconsideration
may return it once more, since the proviso allows reconsideration only on his discretion
may refer it to the Supreme Court and defer action until the opinion is received
may keep it pending indefinitely, in the manner of a pocket veto
questions.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) added the proviso: the President may require reconsideration, but must act on the advice tendered after it (Laxmikanth p.294).
w: The 44th Amendment proviso allows one return only; the reconsidered advice is binding.
Article 74 contains no such reference and no deferral; Article 143 is a separate advisory power.
The pocket veto applies to Bills awaiting assent, not to ministerial advice, which the President 'shall' follow.

questions.q: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha. They are chosen from among persons having special knowledge or practical experience in
questions.a: literature, science, art and social service
o: literature, science, art and social service
literature, science, sports and social service
literature, science, art and public administration
science, art, the cooperative movement and social service
questions.e: The four fields are literature, science, art and social service (Laxmikanth p.284).
w: Sports is not among the fields listed in the Constitution.
Public administration is not a listed field; social service is.
The cooperative movement appears in the list for nominating members to a State Legislative Council, not the Rajya Sabha.
tr: Rajya Sabha vs Legislative Council nominations

questions.q: Article 87(2) provides for rules to allot time to discuss the matters referred to in the President's address. In practice the discussion takes place through
questions.e: The address is discussed through the Motion of Thanks.
w: A Calling Attention Motion draws a Minister's attention to an urgent matter; it is not used for the address.
A short duration discussion is held on a matter of urgent public importance, not on the address.
A Cut Motion belongs to the demands for grants, not the President's address.

questions.q: The 'pocket veto' of the President of India is possible mainly because the Constitution
questions.a: prescribes no time limit within which the President must decide on a Bill presented for assent
o: prescribes no time limit within which the President must decide on a Bill presented for assent
requires the President to return a Bill within ten days
allows the President to prorogue Parliament without the Council's advice
lets the President amend a Bill before giving assent
questions.e: Because Article 111 sets no time limit, the President can keep a Bill pending indefinitely (Laxmikanth p.288).
w: The ten-day limit exists in the American system, not in India (Laxmikanth p.288).
Prorogation is done on ministerial advice and has no bearing on the delay.
The President can only assent, withhold or return a Bill; he cannot amend it.

questions.q: Under which Article may the President give assent to a Bill passed by both Houses of Parliament, whereupon it becomes an Act?
questions.e: Article 111 gives the President the choice to assent, withhold assent or return a Bill (Laxmikanth p.287).
w: Article 108 provides for the joint sitting of the Houses.
Article 110 defines a Money Bill.
Article 112 provides for the annual financial statement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's relationship with the Council of Ministers:

1. The President exercises executive power on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74.
2. Under Article 78 the Prime Minister must communicate to the President all Council decisions on Union administration and proposals for legislation.
3. The Prime Minister must furnish any information on Union administration that the President asks for.
4. If the President so directs, the Prime Minister must submit to the Council a matter that a Minister has decided but the Council has not considered.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President exercises executive power on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74 (Laxmikanth p.294). Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 78 the Prime Minister must communicate to the President all Council decisions on Union administration and proposals for legislation (Laxmikanth p.310). Statement 3 is correct: The Prime Minister must furnish any information on Union administration that the President asks for (Laxmikanth p.310). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.310. So the answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's appointments:

1. The President appoints the Chief Justice and Judges of the Supreme Court, the Attorney General of India and the Comptroller and Auditor General.
2. The President appoints the Governors of States and the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
3. The President appoints the Chief Ministers of the States on the advice of the Governors.
4. The members of the Finance Commission are appointed by the Prime Minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President appoints the Chief Justice and Judges of the Supreme Court, the Attorney General of India and the Comptroller and Auditor General (Laxmikanth p.283). Statement 2 is correct: The President appoints the Governors of States and the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Laxmikanth p.283). Statement 3 is incorrect: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister; the President does not. Statement 4 is incorrect: The President constitutes the Finance Commission and appoints its Chairman and members (Laxmikanth p.283). So the answer is 1 and 2 only.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.62
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's powers over territories and punishments:

1. Administrators appointed by the President run the Union Territories on his behalf.
2. Scheduled Areas are declared by the Governor of the State concerned, and the President has no role in their administration.
3. The clemency power of the President under Article 72 does not extend to sentences passed by a court martial.
4. The President's clemency power under Article 72 covers cases in which the sentence is a sentence of death.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Administrators appointed by the President run the Union Territories on his behalf (Laxmikanth p.283). Statement 2 is incorrect: The President declares Scheduled Areas and has powers over their administration. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 72 expressly covers court-martial sentences, offences against Union law and death sentences (Laxmikanth p.286). Statement 4 is correct: A death sentence is one of the three heads (Laxmikanth p.286). So the answer is 1 and 4 only.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.62

Consider the following statements about the President's role in relation to Parliament:

4. According to Laxmikanth, when the offices of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are vacant, the President may appoint a member of the Rajya Sabha to preside over the Lok Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 85 (Laxmikanth p.284). Statement 2 is incorrect: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides at a joint sitting. Statement 3 is incorrect: He may send messages on a pending Bill or on any other matter (Laxmikanth p.284). Statement 4 is incorrect: The President appoints a member of the Lok Sabha itself (Laxmikanth p.284). So the answer is 1 only.

2. The President also addresses both Houses together at the beginning of the first session of every year.
3. During the Motion of Thanks members may criticise policy, point out omissions and move amendments.
4. The defeat of the Motion of Thanks is regarded as equal to a vote of no-confidence in the Council of Ministers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is delivered after the oath and the election of the Speaker, and sets out the new government's policy objectives and legislative priorities. Statement 2 is correct: The President also addresses both Houses together at the beginning of the first session of every year (Laxmikanth p.284). Statement 3 is correct: During the Motion of Thanks members may criticise policy, point out omissions and move amendments. Statement 4 is correct: . So the answer is 2, 3 and 4 only.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President and Bills passed by Parliament:

1. A Bill passed by the legislature does not become law until the President or the Governor assents to it.
2. On a Money Bill the President may assent or withhold assent but cannot return it.
3. On an ordinary Bill the President may assent or withhold assent but cannot return it for reconsideration.
4. Under Article 111 the President may give assent to a Bill passed by both Houses, whereupon it becomes an Act.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A Bill passed by the legislature does not become law until the President or the Governor assents to it (Laxmikanth p.287). Statement 2 is correct: On a Money Bill the President may assent or withhold assent but cannot return it (Laxmikanth p.288). Statement 3 is incorrect: On an ordinary Bill the President may also return it, and must assent if Parliament passes it again. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.287. So the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.63

Consider the following statements about Bills reserved by a Governor for the President:

1. The State Legislature can override the President's refusal of assent by passing the reserved Bill again.
2. If the Legislature passes a returned Bill again, the President is not bound to give assent, unlike under Article 111.
3. The Constitution prescribes no time limit within which the President must act on a reserved State Bill.
4. The President may direct the Governor to return a reserved Money Bill for reconsideration.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The President's withholding of assent cannot be overridden by the State Legislature. Statement 2 is correct: If the Legislature passes a returned Bill again, the President is not bound to give assent, unlike under Article 111 (Laxmikanth p.289). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.289, which adds that the pocket veto thus applies to State Bills. Statement 4 is incorrect: Only a reserved Bill that is not a Money Bill may be returned. So the answer is 2 and 3 only.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.64
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the types of veto:

1. Absolute veto means withholding assent so that the Bill lapses; it can be used when the Cabinet resigns after a Bill is passed and the new government advises the President not to assent.
2. Suspensive veto is returning a Bill other than a Money Bill to Parliament for reconsideration.
3. The Indian President has no qualified veto; it is an American feature requiring two-thirds of both Houses of Congress to override.
4. The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 made presidential assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill mandatory.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Absolute veto means withholding assent so that the Bill lapses; it can be used when the Cabinet resigns after a Bill is passed and the new government advises the President not to assent (Laxmikanth p.288). Statement 2 is correct: Suspensive veto is returning a Bill other than a Money Bill to Parliament for reconsideration (Laxmikanth p.288). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.288. India avoids it, as commonly explained, to keep legislative supremacy under the parliamentary system. Statement 4 is incorrect: That was done by the 24th Amendment Act, 1971; the 42nd made the Council's advice binding. So the answer is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.64
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.64
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's legislative role:

3. Bills affecting State boundaries and Money Bills need the President's prior recommendation or consent for introduction.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Statement 2 is incorrect: The 104th Amendment Act of 2019 discontinued the provision (Laxmikanth p.284). Statement 4 is incorrect: He decides after consulting the Election Commission (Laxmikanth p.284). So the answer is 1 and 3 only.

3. The President may send messages to a House on a pending Bill or on any other matter.
4. According to Laxmikanth, when the offices of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are vacant, the President may appoint a member of the House to preside.

questions.q:

2. According to Laxmikanth, the President can exercise a pocket veto over State Bills as well, since no time limit is fixed.
3. The Constitution fixes a three-month time limit for the President to decide on a reserved State Bill.
4. When the President assents to a reserved State Bill, it becomes law in that State, subject to the rule on repugnancy with Union law under Article 254.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President's withholding of assent to a reserved State Bill cannot be overridden by the State Legislature (Laxmikanth p.289). Statement 2 is correct: according to Laxmikanth p.289 the President can exercise a pocket veto over State Bills as well, since no time limit is fixed (the point has been contested in the courts since the 2025 rulings). Statement 3 is incorrect: The Constitution prescribes no time limit. Statement 4 is correct: when the President assents to a reserved State Bill it becomes law in that State, subject to the repugnancy rule with Union law under Article 254. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

2. Pocket veto means returning a Bill other than a Money Bill to Parliament for reconsideration.
3. The President may return a Constitution Amendment Bill passed under Article 368 for reconsideration.
4. The President can return a Money Bill with suggestions for amendment.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The executive is not bound to support it (Laxmikanth p.288). Statement 2 is incorrect: That is the suspensive veto; the pocket veto is keeping the Bill pending without action. Statement 3 is incorrect: The President cannot withhold assent, return or delay such a Bill. Statement 4 is incorrect: A Money Bill cannot be returned. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

Consider the following statements:

questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

questions.q:
Match the types of veto in List-I with their description in List-II.

List-I
A. Absolute veto
B. Suspensive veto
C. Pocket veto
D. Qualified veto

List-II
1. Bill kept pending indefinitely without assent or return
2. Assent is withheld and the Bill lapses
3. Bill is returned and a re-passage by ordinary majority forces assent
4. Can be overridden only by a special majority; a feature of the American system
questions.e: Absolute veto kills the Bill; suspensive veto is overridden by an ordinary majority (p.65); pocket veto is inaction (p.65); qualified veto belongs to the American President (p.65). Also Laxmikanth p.287-288.
w: A and B are interchanged: withholding assent is the absolute veto.
B and C are interchanged: returning a Bill is the suspensive veto.
C and D are interchanged: indefinite pending is the pocket veto and the special-majority override is the qualified veto.

concepts.name: Ordinance power, financial, judicial, diplomatic and military powers
concepts.description: Article 123 and the judicial scrutiny of ordinances, the comparison with the Governor's Article 213, regulations for Union Territories, the President's financial, pardoning, diplomatic and military powers.
concepts.idea: An ordinance has the force of an Act, lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved, and can be challenged in court.
concepts.rule: The President may promulgate an ordinance when Parliament is not in session; it must be approved within six weeks of reassembly and may be withdrawn at any time. The cases D.C. Wadhwa, Krishna Kumar Singh, Cooper and T. Venkata Reddy deal with re-promulgation, mala fides and the legislative character of the power. The Governor's counterpart is Article 213, limited to State and Concurrent List subjects and needing presidential instructions in three cases. The President makes regulations for certain Union Territories (Article 240), causes the budget and commission reports to be laid, recommends Money Bills and demands for grants, and constitutes the Finance Commission every five years. Pardon, commutation, remission, respite and reprieve are distinct forms of clemency. He appoints ambassadors and the three service chiefs and is Supreme Commander.
concepts.example: A Governor's ordinance in a unicameral State cannot be promulgated while the Assembly is in session, and a President's cannot be promulgated when both Houses sit.

Article 243 is the first Article of Part IX on Panchayats.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's ordinance power under Article 123:

1. The President may promulgate an ordinance with the force of an Act when Parliament is not in session.
2. An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its promulgation, failing which it lapses.
3. The President has the power to recall an ordinance whenever he chooses before it lapses.
4. An ordinance can be issued even when only one House is in session, but not when both Houses are in session.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President may promulgate an ordinance with the force of an Act when Parliament is not in session (Laxmikanth p.290). Statement 2 is incorrect: The six weeks run from the reassembly of Parliament, not from promulgation. Statement 3 is correct: The President has the power to recall an ordinance whenever he chooses before it lapses (Laxmikanth p.292). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.290, since a law needs both Houses. So the answer is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.65
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.65

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial scrutiny of ordinances:

1. Repeated re-promulgation of ordinances without placing them before the legislature has been held unconstitutional in the D.C. Wadhwa case.
2. In the Cooper case the Supreme Court held that the President's satisfaction in issuing an ordinance cannot be questioned in any court.
3. In Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017) the Supreme Court treated re-promulgation without placing the ordinance before the legislature as a fraud on the Constitution.
4. In T. Venkata Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh the Court held the ordinance-making power to be executive and free of the limits that bind laws.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Repeated re-promulgation of ordinances without placing them before the legislature has been held unconstitutional in the D.C. Wadhwa case (Laxmikanth p.292). Statement 2 is incorrect: The Court held that it can be questioned on the ground of mala fides (Laxmikanth p.290-291). Statement 3 is correct: In Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017) the Supreme Court treated re-promulgation without placing the ordinance before the legislature as a fraud on the Constitution. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Court held the power to be legislative in character and subject to the same limits as laws. So the answer is 1 and 3 only.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.65
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.65
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.65

Consider the following statements about ordinances:

1. An ordinance can be challenged as colourable legislation.
2. An ordinance that violates a Fundamental Right can be challenged.
3. An ordinance may be used to amend the Constitution if the urgency is shown.
4. The ordinance-making power is legislative in character even though it is exercised by the executive.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: An ordinance can be challenged as colourable legislation. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.291 adds that the definition of 'law' in Article 13 includes ordinances. Statement 3 is incorrect: An ordinance cannot be issued to amend the Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: an ordinance has the same force as an Act of Parliament (Laxmikanth p.291). So the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.65
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.65

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Statement 2 is correct: The President can legislate by ordinance on Union and Concurrent List subjects, the Governor on State and Concurrent List subjects. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is reversed: the President needs no prior instruction, while the Governor needs the President's instructions in three cases. Statement 4 is correct: . So the answer is 2 and 4 only.

Consider the following statements about the ordinance powers of the President and the Governor:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: In both cases the ordinance has the force of an Act, must be laid before the legislature and ceases six weeks after reassembly unless approved (Laxmikanth p.291). Statement 2 is correct: Neither the President nor the Governor can use an ordinance to amend the Constitution (Laxmikanth p.292). questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's judicial powers:

1. The President appoints the Chief Justice and Judges of the Supreme Court under Article 124 and Judges of High Courts under Article 217.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Statement 2 is incorrect: Pardon removes both the sentence and the conviction and restores civil rights. Statement 3 is correct: Commutation substitutes a lighter form of punishment for a heavier one, such as a death sentence by life imprisonment (Laxmikanth p.293). Statement 4 is incorrect: Remission reduces the duration without changing its nature; changing the kind of punishment is commutation. So the answer is 1 and 3 only.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Statement 4 is correct: . So the answer is 4 only.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ordinances:

1. Both the President's and the Governor's ordinance powers are co-extensive with the law-making power of Parliament or the State Legislature.
2. A Governor may legislate by ordinance on a subject in the Union List if the matter is urgent.
3. Both the President and the Governor must be satisfied that circumstances require immediate action.
4. The President promulgates an ordinance on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Both the President's and the Governor's ordinance powers are co-extensive with the law-making power of Parliament or the State Legislature (Laxmikanth p.291). Statement 2 is incorrect: The Governor is confined to State and Concurrent List subjects. Statement 3 is correct: Both the President and the Governor must be satisfied that circumstances require immediate action. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.292. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. For Puducherry the President can make regulations only when its Legislative Assembly is dissolved or suspended.
2. The President constitutes a Finance Commission after every five years or earlier, under Article 280.
3. The Finance Commission recommends the sharing of tax revenue between the Centre and the States, the principles of grants-in-aid and measures to strengthen State finances.
4. The President makes advances for unforeseen expenditure out of the Contingency Fund of India.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: For Puducherry the President can make regulations only when its Legislative Assembly is dissolved or suspended. Statement 2 is correct: (Article 280). Statement 3 is correct: The Finance Commission recommends the sharing of tax revenue between the Centre and the States, the principles of grants-in-aid and measures to strengthen State finances. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.285. So all four statements are correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about clemency:

1. A pardon removes both the sentence and the conviction.
2. Commutation reduces the duration of a sentence without changing its nature.
3. Respite is a temporary stay of the execution of a death sentence.
4. The Governor can pardon a sentence of death imposed under a State law.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A pardon removes both the sentence and the conviction (Laxmikanth p.292). Statement 2 is incorrect: That is remission; commutation changes the form of punishment to a lighter one. Statement 3 is incorrect: That is reprieve; respite gives a lesser sentence because of special facts such as pregnancy. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence or a court-martial sentence, though he can suspend, remit or commute a death sentence (Laxmikanth p.293). So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The President cannot validly promulgate an ordinance while both Houses of Parliament are in session.
Statement-II: An ordinance is meant to meet a situation requiring immediate action when Parliament is not available to legislate.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: (Laxmikanth p.290, which says an ordinance made when both Houses are in session is void). Statement-II is correct: and gives the reason: the power exists for the recess, so it is not a parallel power of legislation.
w: Statement-II is the actual reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: An ordinance ceases to operate six weeks after Parliament reassembles, unless Parliament approves it.
Statement-II: An ordinance can be recalled by the President whenever he chooses.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct (Laxmikanth p.291-292). Statement-II is a separate power of the President and does not explain the six-week lapse.
w: Statement-II is correct but it is not the reason for Statement-I; they are separate facts.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the cases in List-I with their holdings or findings in List-II.

List-I
A. D.C. Wadhwa
B. Krishna Kumar Singh
C. R.C. Cooper
D. T. Venkata Reddy

List-II
1. Ordinance-making is a legislative power of the executive
2. The executive's satisfaction behind an ordinance is open to challenge for mala fides
3. Re-promulgation without placing the ordinance before the legislature is a fraud on the Constitution
4. Successive re-promulgation of a Governor's ordinances without trying to get the Bills passed is unconstitutional
questions.e: Wadhwa: Laxmikanth p.292; Krishna Kumar Singh: Cooper: Laxmikanth p.290-291; Venkata Reddy.
w: A and B are interchanged: Wadhwa concerned a Governor's repeated re-promulgation; the 'fraud on the Constitution' words are from Krishna Kumar Singh.
C and D are interchanged: Cooper concerned the mala fides test, Venkata Reddy the legislative nature of the power.
