concepts.name: Presidential discretion and immunities; the Vice-President's election, term, removal and vacancy
concepts.description: Emergency powers, situational discretion, immunities under Article 361, and the Vice-President's qualifications, electoral college, term, removal and vacancy.
concepts.idea: The President has only situational discretion and personal immunity, while the Vice-President is elected by Parliament alone and removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution.
concepts.rule: The emergency powers are in Part XVIII and are exercised on ministerial advice. The President uses discretion in a hung House, on sudden vacancy of the Prime Minister's office and in dissolving the Lok Sabha after loss of majority. Article 361 bars criminal proceedings during the term and requires two months' notice for civil suits on personal acts. The Vice-President must be a citizen of 35 years qualified for the Rajya Sabha and is elected by all MPs, elected and nominated, by STV; nomination needs 20 proposers and 20 seconders and a Rs 15,000 deposit under the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 as amended in 1997. The term is five years from entering office; removal is by a Rajya Sabha resolution on 14 days' notice, with no ground named. Article 68 requires the election before expiry of the term or as soon as possible after other vacancies, and the person elected gets a full term.
concepts.example: A Vice-President who dies in office is replaced by an election held as soon as possible, not within six months, and the successor serves five full years.

questions.q: The emergency powers of the President, which he exercises on ministerial advice and which are subject to parliamentary and judicial safeguards, are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.e: The emergency provisions form Part XVIII (Laxmikanth p.286-287 lists the three types).
w: Part XVII deals with the official language.
Part XIX is the Miscellaneous part.
Part XX deals with the amendment of the Constitution.

questions.q: Article 361(1) shields the President from answering to any court for the exercise of his powers and duties. His conduct can nevertheless be reviewed by a court, tribunal or body appointed by a House of Parliament for investigating a charge under which Article?
questions.e: Article 61 is the impeachment procedure; a body investigating a charge under it can examine the President's conduct, so the immunity is functional, not absolute (Laxmikanth p.295 table lists Article 61).
w: Article 56 deals with the President's term.
Article 67 deals with the term and removal of the Vice-President.
Article 124 deals with the Supreme Court and its Judges, not with presidential conduct.

questions.q: The nomination of a candidate for the Vice-Presidency must be subscribed by electors as proposers and seconders. The required number is
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.303 gives 20 and 20 for the Vice-President; the figure is 50 and 50 for the President.
w: Ten each was the presidential figure before 1997.
There is no figure of 25 for either office.
Fifty each is the requirement for a presidential candidate (Laxmikanth p.280), not for a Vice-Presidential one.

questions.q: A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be introduced only in
o: a joint sitting of both Houses
questions.e: The resolution can originate only in the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha (Laxmikanth p.304).
w: The Lok Sabha only agrees to the resolution.
Unlike the impeachment of the President, which either House may initiate, the Vice-President's removal resolution is confined to one House.
A joint sitting is not used for this purpose.

questions.q: An election to fill a casual vacancy in the Vice-President's office, and the term of the person elected, are provided for in
questions.e: Article 68 covers the time of election and the term of a person elected to fill a casual vacancy (Laxmikanth p.306).
w: Article 62 is the corresponding provision for the President.
Article 67 deals with the term of office of the Vice-President.
Article 69 deals with the oath or affirmation of the Vice-President.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the President's situational discretion:

1. The President uses discretion in appointing the Prime Minister when no party or coalition has a clear majority in the Lok Sabha.
2. The President uses discretion in appointing the Prime Minister when the office falls vacant by sudden death with no obvious successor.
3. The President is bound to dissolve the Lok Sabha on the advice of a Council of Ministers that has lost its majority.
4. In a hung House the President cannot ask the person he invites to prove a majority on the floor of the House.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President uses discretion in appointing the Prime Minister when no party or coalition has a clear majority in the Lok Sabha (Laxmikanth p.295). Statement 2 is correct: The President uses discretion in appointing the Prime Minister when the office falls vacant by sudden death with no obvious successor (Laxmikanth p.295). Statement 3 is incorrect: He may dissolve at his discretion when no alternative government appears viable, and need not oblige a Council that has lost confidence (Laxmikanth p.318). Statement 4 is incorrect: He invites the leader likeliest to command the House's confidence and may require a floor test within a reasonable time (Laxmikanth p.308). So the answer is 1 and 2 only.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.69
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.69
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the immunities of the President:

1. Article 361(1) makes the President not answerable to any court for the exercise of his powers and duties.
2. The President's conduct can be reviewed by a body appointed by a House of Parliament to investigate a charge under Article 61.
3. Criminal proceedings already begun may continue against the President during his term, though he cannot be arrested.
4. The notice for a civil suit on a personal act must state the nature of the proceedings, the cause of action, the relief sought and the identity of the parties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.281 (personal immunity for official acts). Statement 2 is correct: The President's conduct can be reviewed by a body appointed by a House of Parliament to investigate a charge under Article 61. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 361(2) bars criminal proceedings from being instituted or continued during his term, and he cannot be arrested, detained, imprisoned, summoned or have a warrant issued. Statement 4 is correct: . So the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.69
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.69
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President's office and qualifications:

1. The Vice-President occupies the second highest constitutional office and ranks next to the President in the warrant of precedence.
2. Like the American Vice-President, the Indian Vice-President succeeds to the presidency for the unexpired term when it falls vacant.
3. A Vice-Presidential candidate must be an Indian citizen of at least 35 years who is qualified for election as a Rajya Sabha member.
4. A candidate must not hold an office of profit under the Union Government, a State Government, or a local or other authority under government control.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Vice-President occupies the second highest constitutional office and ranks next to the President in the warrant of precedence (Laxmikanth p.301). Statement 2 is incorrect: He only acts as President until a new President enters office (Laxmikanth p.305). Statement 3 is correct: A Vice-Presidential candidate must be an Indian citizen of at least 35 years who is qualified for election as a Rajya Sabha member (Laxmikanth p.303). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.303. So the answer is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.69
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.69
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of the Vice-President:

1. The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament by proportional representation using a single transferable vote with secret ballot.
2. The members of State Legislative Assemblies are part of the electoral college, as in the presidential election.
3. Only the elected members of the two Houses of Parliament form the electoral college.
4. Doubts and disputes about the election of the Vice-President are decided by the Election Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament by proportional representation using a single transferable vote with secret ballot (Laxmikanth p.301). Statement 2 is incorrect: The college consists of the members of both Houses of Parliament only. Statement 3 is incorrect: The college includes nominated members as well as elected ones (Laxmikanth p.301). Statement 4 is incorrect: They are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final (Laxmikanth p.301). So the answer is 1 only.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.70
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.70
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President's term:

1. The term of five years runs from the date of the election result.
2. He continues in office after the term ends until his successor enters upon office.
3. He may resign by writing addressed to the President.
4. He is eligible for re-election, with no limit on the number of terms.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It runs from the date the Vice-President enters upon office, not the date of election. Statement 2 is correct: He continues in office after the term ends until his successor enters upon office (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 3 is correct: He may resign by writing addressed to the President (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.304 (Dr S. Radhakrishnan served a second term). So the answer is 2, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.70
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.70
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the Vice-President:

1. Removal begins with a Rajya Sabha resolution backed by a majority of all its then members, to which the Lok Sabha must agree.
2. In the Lok Sabha a two-thirds majority of members present and voting is required to agree to the resolution.
3. The resolution can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha.
4. The Constitution names 'violation of the Constitution' as the ground for removing the Vice-President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.304 (an effective majority in the Rajya Sabha). Statement 2 is incorrect: A simple majority is sufficient in the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: The resolution can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 4 is incorrect: No ground is specified for the Vice-President; 'violation of the Constitution' is the ground for impeaching the President. So the answer is 1 and 3 only.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.70
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.70
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about vacancy in the office of the Vice-President:

1. The office falls vacant on expiry of the term, resignation or removal.
2. Death of the Vice-President is also a cause of vacancy.
3. Disqualification and annulment of the election by the Supreme Court are also causes of vacancy.
4. The President can remove the Vice-President on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The office falls vacant on expiry of the term, resignation or removal (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.304 and its footnote on p.306 (Krishna Kant was the first Vice-President to die in office). Statement 3 is correct: Disqualification and annulment of the election by the Supreme Court are also causes of vacancy (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 4 is incorrect: Removal is only by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha agreed to by the Lok Sabha. So the answer is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.71
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.71
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.71

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election to fill a vacancy in the office of the Vice-President:

1. Article 69 governs the time of holding an election to fill such a vacancy.
2. If the vacancy is due to expiry of the term, the election must be completed before the term expires.
3. A person elected to fill a vacancy holds office for a full five-year term from entering office.
4. Article 68 sets a mandatory six-month limit for filling a vacancy, as Article 62 does for the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 69 prescribes the oath; the election timing is under Article 68. Statement 2 is correct: If the vacancy is due to expiry of the term, the election must be completed before the term expires (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 3 is correct: A person elected to fill a vacancy holds office for a full five-year term from entering office (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 68 sets no mandatory six-month limit; the election is held as soon as possible. So the answer is 2 and 3 only.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.71
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.71
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.71

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The emergency powers of the President in Part XVIII are exercised on ministerial advice and are subject to parliamentary and judicial safeguards.
2. A notice of at least 14 days must be given before a resolution for the removal of the Vice-President is moved.
3. The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha at his discretion when the Council of Ministers has lost its majority and no alternative government seems viable.
4. By virtue of his office the Vice-President presides over the Rajya Sabha as its Chairman.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The emergency powers of the President in Part XVIII are exercised on ministerial advice and are subject to parliamentary and judicial safeguards. Statement 2 is correct: A notice of at least 14 days must be given before a resolution for the removal of the Vice-President is moved (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.295 lists dissolution after loss of majority as situational discretion. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.305. So the answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.68
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.68
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.68

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about proceedings against the President:

1. Article 361(2) bars criminal proceedings from being instituted or continued against the President during his term, and he cannot be arrested.
2. Civil suits for the President's personal acts can be filed during his term only after two months' written notice.
3. Article 361(1) makes the President answerable to the courts for the exercise of his official powers after due notice.
4. The notice must state the nature of the proceedings, the cause of action, the relief sought and the identity of the parties.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 361(2) bars criminal proceedings from being instituted or continued against the President during his term, and he cannot be arrested (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 2 is correct: Civil suits for the President's personal acts can be filed during his term only after two months' written notice (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 3 is incorrect: He is not answerable to any court for his official acts. Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the nomination of a candidate for the Vice-Presidency:

1. The college of electors consists of elected and nominated Members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. Fifty proposers and fifty seconders are demanded of a Vice-Presidential nominee.
3. A Vice-Presidential candidate lodges a security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the Reserve Bank of India.
4. The nomination rules come from the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1997.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The college of electors consists of elected and nominated Members of both Houses of Parliament (Laxmikanth p.301). Statement 2 is incorrect: The Vice-Presidential figure is 20 and 20; 50 and 50 is for the President. Statement 3 is correct: A Vice-Presidential candidate lodges a security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the Reserve Bank of India (Laxmikanth p.303). Statement 4 is incorrect: The Act is of 1952, as amended in 1997 (Laxmikanth p.303 footnote 3); the 1997 amendment raised the numbers of proposers and seconders. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. If the Vice-President's office falls vacant by death, the election must be held within six months of the vacancy.
2. A person elected to fill the vacancy serves the balance of the predecessor's term.
3. Article 69 prescribes the time within which an election to fill a vacancy must be held.
4. If the vacancy is due to expiry of the term, the election may be held within six months after the term ends.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 68 prescribes no six-month limit; the election is held as soon as possible (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 2 is incorrect: The person gets a full five-year term (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 69 prescribes the oath; the election is governed by Article 68 (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement 4 is incorrect: It must be completed before the term expires, so that there is no interregnum. So no statement is correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 0 of the four statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 0 of the four statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 0 of the four statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Vice-President can be removed from office without a formal impeachment.
Statement-II: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Vice-President is removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha, not by impeachment (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement-II is correct: Article 64 makes him ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Laxmikanth p.305). His chairmanship has no bearing on the manner of his removal, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Statement-II describes his role in the House; it is not the reason removal is by resolution rather than impeachment.
Statement-II is correct (Article 64), so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A person elected to fill a mid-term vacancy in the Vice-President's office holds office for a full five-year term.
Statement-II: Article 68 requires such an election to be held within six months of the vacancy.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: A person elected to fill a mid-term vacancy in the Vice-President's office holds office for a full five-year term (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement-II is incorrect: Article 68 sets no mandatory six-month limit, unlike Article 62 for the President; the election is held as soon as possible.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is not correct, so the 'both correct' options fail.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the item in List-I with the period or amount in List-II.

List-I
A. Notice before a civil suit on a personal act of the President
B. Notice before moving a resolution for the removal of the Vice-President
C. Security deposit of a Vice-Presidential candidate with the Reserve Bank of India
D. Term of the Vice-President

List-II
1. Rs 15,000
2. 14 days
3. Two months
4. Five years
questions.e: Two months' notice; 14 days' notice (p.70); Rs 15,000 deposit (p.70); five-year term (p.70). Also Laxmikanth p.281, 303-304.
w: A and B are interchanged: the civil-suit notice is two months and the removal notice 14 days.
C and D are interchanged: the deposit is Rs 15,000 and the term five years.
B and C are interchanged: the removal notice is 14 days and the deposit Rs 15,000.

concepts.name: Vice-President's oath, functions and salary; Prime Minister's appointment and relationship with the President
concepts.description: The Vice-President's oath, Rajya Sabha chairmanship, acting presidency and salary, the appointment of the Prime Minister, collective responsibility and Article 78.
concepts.idea: The Vice-President presides over the Rajya Sabha and acts as President only until a new President is elected, while the Prime Minister is the real executive and accountable to Parliament.
concepts.rule: The Vice-President takes his oath before the President or a person appointed by him, cannot be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature and holds no office of profit. As ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64 he decides procedure and has only a casting vote. Under Article 65 he acts as President for at most six months on a vacancy and without a time limit during the President's temporary incapacity, with the President's emoluments; otherwise he draws only the Chairman's salary under Article 97. The Prime Minister is appointed under Article 75(1), may belong to either House, and advises the President on key appointments. Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha means ministers support Cabinet decisions or resign; Article 78 obliges the Prime Minister to inform the President.
concepts.example: Manmohan Singh was a Rajya Sabha member when he became Prime Minister in 2004, which the British convention would not allow.

questions.q: The oath or affirmation of the Vice-President under Article 69 is administered by
questions.a: the President or a person appointed by him for the purpose
o: the President or a person appointed by him for the purpose
the Chief Justice of India, as in the case of the President
the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.303 and the: the President, or a person he appoints, administers the oath.

concepts.name: Prime Minister's oath, tenure and powers; PMO; Deputy PM; advice of the Council
concepts.description: The Prime Minister's oath and secrecy, tenure, salary, powers in relation to the Council, Parliament and others, the PMO, the Deputy Prime Minister and the legal position of ministerial advice.
concepts.idea: The Prime Minister holds office as long as he has Lok Sabha confidence, and the Council's advice binds the President after at most one reconsideration.
concepts.rule: The Prime Minister takes the oaths of office and secrecy under Article 75(4) in the Third Schedule. He has no fixed term, cannot be dismissed while he has a majority, and receives an MP's salary plus a sumptuary allowance. He recommends ministers, allocates portfolios, presides over the Council and brings it down by resigning, leads the Lok Sabha and chairs bodies such as NITI Aayog. The PMO is not in the Constitution and is headed by the Principal Secretary; the Deputy Prime Minister post is conventional. The 91st Amendment caps the Council at 15 per cent of Lok Sabha strength and bars defectors from office; the 42nd Amendment made advice binding and the 44th allowed one reconsideration; Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into the advice; the Council continues after dissolution (U.N.R. Rao).
concepts.example: A Prime Minister who loses a vote of confidence must resign, but the President cannot dismiss one who commands a majority.

concepts.name: Council of Ministers, Cabinet, Kitchen Cabinet, Cabinet Committees and Groups of Ministers
concepts.description: Appointment, oath, salary and responsibility of ministers, the three categories, the Cabinet and the Kitchen Cabinet, the Cabinet Committees and Groups of Ministers.
concepts.idea: The Council has three ranks, the Cabinet is its inner part inserted in Article 352 in 1978, and the Cabinet works through committees that the Constitution does not mention.
concepts.rule: Ministers are appointed by the President on the Prime Minister's advice and a non-member must enter Parliament within six months. Parliament fixes their salaries. Collective responsibility is inferred from Article 75(3), individual responsibility from the pleasure of the President, and neither creates legal liability. The Council has Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers; the Cabinet was inserted into Article 352 by the 44th Amendment and consists of Cabinet Ministers only. The Kitchen Cabinet is informal and extra-constitutional. Cabinet Committees (Political Affairs, called the Super-Cabinet, Economic Affairs, Appointments, Parliamentary Affairs, Security, Accommodation, Investment and Growth, Employment and Skill Development) are set up by the Prime Minister; Groups of Ministers are ad hoc.
concepts.example: A Minister of State with independent charge runs a ministry like a Cabinet Minister but attends Cabinet meetings only when invited.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

A. Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs

concepts.name: President and Vice-President compared; Council of Ministers and Attorney General
concepts.description: A revision of the table comparing the offices of President and Vice-President: Articles, electoral college, method, term, removal, roles, plus the Council's responsibility and the Attorney General.
concepts.idea: The two offices differ in the electoral college and the manner of removal but share the method of election and the five-year term.
concepts.rule: The President is governed by Articles 52-62 and the Vice-President by Articles 63-71. The President's electoral college has elected MPs and elected MLAs; the Vice-President's has all MPs, elected and nominated, and no MLAs. Both are elected by STV through secret ballot and hold five-year terms. The President is impeached for violation of the Constitution by two-thirds of the total membership of each House; the Vice-President is removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by simple majority. The President is Supreme Commander and the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, and the Attorney General under Article 76 may take part in Parliament's proceedings without a vote.
concepts.example: State legislators vote in the presidential election but not in the vice-presidential one, because the Vice-President's normal work is to preside over the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: The office of the President is governed by Articles 52 to 62 of the Constitution. The provisions on the office of the Vice-President are contained in
questions.e: The Vice-President's block is Articles 63-71 (Laxmikanth p.305-306 table).
w: Articles 72 to 75 deal with the President's pardoning power, the Council of Ministers and the Prime Minister's appointment, not the Vice-President.
Article 63 is the first Article, creating the office; the block starts there.
Articles 72 to 74 deal with the pardoning power and the Council of Ministers, not the Vice-President.

questions.q: The electoral college for the election of the Vice-President consists of
questions.a: the elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament
o: the elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament
only the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, with all nominated members excluded
the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
the members of the Rajya Sabha, elected and nominated, together with the members of the State Legislative Councils
questions.e: The Vice-President's electoral college consists of all members of both Houses of Parliament, nominated members included (Laxmikanth p.301).
w: The college includes nominated members too (Laxmikanth p.301).
That combination is the electoral college for the President, not the Vice-President.
Lok Sabha members are in the college, and State Legislature members are not.

questions.q: When the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers, those who must resign are
questions.a: all the Ministers, including those who are members of the Rajya Sabha
o: all the Ministers, including those who are members of the Rajya Sabha
only the Ministers who are members of the Lok Sabha
only the Cabinet Ministers, while Ministers of State may continue
only the Prime Minister, since the Council is not collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: Article 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha alone, yet Rajya Sabha Ministers also resign on a no-confidence vote (Laxmikanth p.318).
w: The responsibility is joint, so Rajya Sabha members of the Council also go.
The responsibility is collective, covering every category of Minister.
The Prime Minister's resignation amounts to the resignation of the whole Council, but all Ministers fall with the vote.

questions.q: According to Laxmikanth, who was the first Vice-President to die in office?
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.306 footnote 5; Krishna Kant was elected in 1997 and died in office.

G.S. Pathak completed his term.
B.D. Jatti acted as President on the death of F.A. Ahmed but did not die in office.

questions.q: Who is the only person to have held the office of President of India for two terms?
questions.e: No person except Dr Rajendra Prasad has occupied the office for two terms (Laxmikanth p.300 footnote 6), though Article 57 sets no limit (on the five-year term).
w: Dr S. Radhakrishnan was elected Vice-President twice but President only once.
R. Venkataraman served one term as President after being Vice-President.
V.V. Giri served a single term.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of the President and the Vice-President:

1. Both are elected by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote through secret ballot.
2. Members of a State Legislative Assembly that has been dissolved continue to vote in the presidential election until fresh elections are held.
3. An election cannot be challenged on the ground that the electoral college was incomplete because of vacancies.
4. Doubts and disputes about either election are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.277 and p.301. Statement 2 is incorrect: Where an Assembly is dissolved, its members cease to be qualified to vote even if fresh elections have not been held (Laxmikanth p.276). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.278 and p.301. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.278 and p.301. So the answer is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.80
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.80
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about qualifications for the two offices:

1. A presidential candidate must be qualified for election to the Lok Sabha, whereas a Vice-Presidential candidate must be qualified for election to the Rajya Sabha.
2. A Vice-Presidential candidate's nomination needs 50 electors as proposers and 50 as seconders.
3. The security deposit is Rs 10,000 for the President and Rs 15,000 for the Vice-President.
4. A Governor of a State or a Union Minister is deemed to hold an office of profit, and so cannot be a candidate.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280 and p.303. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Vice-Presidential figure is 20 and 20; 50 and 50 is for the President. Statement 3 is incorrect: Both candidates deposit Rs 15,000 with the Reserve Bank of India. Statement 4 is incorrect: Laxmikanth p.280 and p.303: a President, Vice-President, Governor or Union or State Minister is not deemed to hold an office of profit. So the answer is 1 only.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.280
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.280
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.280

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the terms of the two offices:

1. Both the President and the Vice-President hold office for five years from the date they enter upon office.
2. The Vice-President's term is counted from the date of his election, but the President's from the date he enters office.
3. Each continues in office after the term until his successor assumes charge.
4. Each is eligible for re-election for one further term, as in the United States.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.281 and p.304. Statement 2 is incorrect: Both are counted from the date of entering office. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.281 and p.304. Statement 4 is incorrect: Each is eligible for re-election any number of times; the two-term limit is an American rule (Laxmikanth p.281 and p.304). So the answer is 1 and 3 only.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.80
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.80
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about removal:

1. The President is removed by impeachment under Article 61 for violation of the Constitution.
2. The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and may be removed by him at any time.
3. An impeachment of the President can be initiated in the Lok Sabha but not in the Rajya Sabha.
4. A resolution to impeach the President must be signed by one-fourth of the House and 14 days' notice given to the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President is removed by impeachment under Article 61 for violation of the Constitution (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 2 is correct: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and may be removed by him at any time (Laxmikanth p.640). Statement 3 is incorrect: It can be initiated in either House (Laxmikanth p.281). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.281. So the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.80
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.80
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President as acting President:

1. The President is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces and the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. Like the American Vice-President, the Indian Vice-President completes the unexpired term of the President when the office falls vacant.
3. If the offices of both the President and the Vice-President are vacant, the Chief Justice of India acts as President.
4. The Vice-President may act as President for up to one year.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces and the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: He acts only until a new President assumes charge (Laxmikanth p.305). Statement 3 is correct: If the offices of both the President and the Vice-President are vacant, the Chief Justice of India acts as President (Laxmikanth p.282). Statement 4 is incorrect: The limit is six months, within which a new President must be elected (Laxmikanth p.305). So the answer is 1 and 3 only.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.80
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.80
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Council of Ministers and the Attorney General:

1. Ministers answer jointly to the Lok Sabha, the House of the People, for their acts.
2. The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under Article 74.
3. The Attorney General is not a member of Parliament but may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House without a vote.
4. The resignation of the Prime Minister amounts to the resignation of the whole Council, including Ministers from the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Ministers answer jointly to the Lok Sabha, the House of the People, for their acts (Laxmikanth p.318). Statement 2 is incorrect: The office is under Article 76. Statement 3 is correct: The Attorney General is not a member of Parliament but may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House without a vote (Laxmikanth p.641). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.318 footnote 3. So the answer is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.80
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.80
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about filling vacancies:

1. A vacancy in the office of President caused by death or resignation must be filled by an election within six months.
2. A vacancy in the office of Vice-President caused by death or resignation is filled as soon as possible.
3. An election to fill a Vice-Presidential vacancy must be held within three months.
4. A person elected to fill a presidential vacancy serves the unexpired part of the predecessor's term.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.282. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.304. Statement 3 is incorrect: No fixed period is prescribed; the election is held as soon as possible. Statement 4 is incorrect: He remains in office for a full term of five years (Laxmikanth p.282). So the answer is 1 and 2 only.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.282
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.282
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.282

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the oaths and conditions of the two offices:

1. The President's oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India.
2. The Vice-President swears to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution and to discharge his duties faithfully.
3. The emoluments and allowances of the President can be diminished by Parliament during his term.
4. Neither the President nor the Vice-President can be a member of Parliament or of a State Legislature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.303. Statement 3 is incorrect: They cannot be diminished during his term of office (Laxmikanth p.280). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280 and p.304. So the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.280
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.280
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.280

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 11th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1961 replaced the joint meeting of Parliament by an electoral college for electing the Vice-President.
2. Ambedkar explained that State legislators vote for the President because his power extends to the administration of the States as well as the Centre.
3. Dr Zakir Husain and Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed died in office as President.
4. Krishna Kant was the first Vice-President to die in office.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.301 footnote 1. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.301. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.300 footnote 7. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.306 footnote 5. So the answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.301
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.301
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.301

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The President and the Vice-President both hold a five-year term.
2. They are elected by the same electoral college.
3. A minimum age of 40 years applies to both offices.
4. Both are elected by a simple plurality of votes.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President and the Vice-President both hold a five-year term. Statement 2 is incorrect: The college for the Vice-President excludes State Legislative Assembly members. Statement 3 is incorrect: The minimum age is 35 years for both offices. Statement 4 is incorrect: Both are elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the oaths:

1. The President's oath includes a promise to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and to serve the well-being of the people.
2. The Vice-President swears to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution.
3. The Vice-President's oath is administered by the President or a person appointed by him.
4. Any other person acting as President or discharging his functions also takes a similar oath.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.303. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.303. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.280. So all four statements are correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 4 of the four statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:

1. The Attorney General must be a person qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. The Attorney General has the right to vote in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha.
3. The Constitution fixes the Attorney General's term of office at five years.
4. The Attorney General is not debarred from private legal practice.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.640. Statement 2 is incorrect: He may speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses and their committees but has no right to vote (Laxmikanth p.641). Statement 3 is incorrect: The term is not fixed by the Constitution; he holds office during the pleasure of the President (Laxmikanth p.640). Statement 4 is correct: He is not a full-time counsel or a government servant (Laxmikanth p.641). So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the four statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the four statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the four statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The members of State Legislative Assemblies take part in the election of the President but not of the Vice-President.
Statement-II: The President's power extends to the administration of the States as well as the Centre, while the Vice-President's normal function is to preside over the Rajya Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The members of State Legislative Assemblies take part in the election of the President but not of the Vice-President (Laxmikanth p.301). Statement-II is correct: and is Ambedkar's reason in the Constituent Assembly, so it explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II is the actual reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Vice-President is removed from office by the process of impeachment, like the President.
Statement-II: The Vice-President is removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: no formal impeachment is required for the Vice-President (Laxmikanth p.304). Statement-II is correct: The Vice-President is removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority.
w: Statement-I is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain it.
Statement-I is not correct, so the 'both correct' options fail.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the offices or processes in List-I with the corresponding feature in List-II.

List-I
A. Electoral college for the President
B. Electoral college for the Vice-President
C. Removal of the President
D. Removal of the Vice-President

List-II
1. Elected MPs together with the elected MLAs of the States, Delhi and Puducherry
2. Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament
3. Impeachment resolution passed in each House by two-thirds of its total membership
4. Rajya Sabha resolution by effective majority, agreed to by the Lok Sabha by simple majority
questions.e: table (corrected for the nominated members of the Vice-President's college); Laxmikanth p.276, 281, 301, 304.
w: A and B are interchanged: the President's college includes the State Assemblies' elected members.
C and D are interchanged: impeachment is for the President; the Rajya Sabha resolution is for the Vice-President.
